source.title: Open problems on cycling in genetic systems

trace.notes: Normalized the input as a zbMATH resolver URL. Direct zbMATH page fetching returned a blocked_or_challenged 403/Cloudflare response, so the official zbMATH API was used for identity recovery. The API identified zbMATH document 2164370 / Zbl 1060.39500 as 'Open problems on cycling in genetic systems' by Robert J. Sacker and Hubertus F. von Bremen, published in Difference and differential equations, Fields Institute Communications 42, pages 435-436 (2004). An exact-title Crossref query recovered DOI 10.1090/fic/042/39 for the same title, authors, source, and pages.

No doc_map was constructed because no readable PDF or full HTML primary source artifact was recovered. The AMS DOI landing/PDF endpoint for https://www.ams.org/fic/042/39 redirected to LibLynx institutional or individual login, and https://www.ams.org/books/fic/042/fic042-39.pdf also redirected to access control. OpenAlex confirmed the same DOI but reported open_access.is_oa=false, oa_status=closed, oa_url=null, and any_repository_has_fulltext=false. Exact-work searches found the AMS bookstore table of contents, an author publication list, bookseller/library table-of-contents pages, and a Trinity repository post-print for a different chapter in the same volume; these were rejected because they were metadata, tables of contents, or a different work.

Moved the run to needs_review under the source-adequacy gate. The recovered materials did not expose the verbatim technical problem statements, so extracting questions from resolver metadata, table-of-contents entries, snippets, or related works would violate the evidence-coverage, evidence-completeness, source-adequacy, and no-new-facts requirements.
Saved the exact JSON payload to outputs/parse-paper/zbmath-2164370.json and updated outputs/latest.json.
